1.why: Every screen uses a clean sans-serif typeface with visibly widened letter spacing and relaxed line height (e.g., the two-line intro on the sign-in page), which is legible and generously spaced.

2.why: No italics, all-caps strings, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; all copy is short title-case or sentence-case text of at most two lines per block.

3.why: The interface is a single narrow column with large text, full-width buttons, and ample whitespace, remaining clearly readable at the mobile width shown in every screenshot.

4.why: Instructions are brief and plain throughout, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code.' and 'Save them somewhere private.'

5.why: Each code field shows the expected format as a placeholder: 'Example: 123456' for identity/authenticator codes and 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for the recovery code.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two short sentences, so the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The long setup secret has a 'Copy setup secret' button and the recovery-code list has 'Copy all codes', so long strings can be copied instead of typed.

8.why: A 'Show QR setup pattern' button reveals a large scannable QR code as an alternative to manual secret entry, with a fallback note if scanning is difficult.

9.why: The screenshots show only plain email/text inputs with no visible autofill interaction, one-time-code autocomplete hint, or password-manager affordance, so support is neither demonstrated nor contradicted.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar, bold heading, and single high-contrast blue button make the current step and primary action obvious on every screen.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one prominent blue primary button while all other options are demoted to grey secondary buttons or small text links.

12.why: Green status banners plainly state what happened and what comes next, e.g. 'Identity checked. Next, set up your authenticator.' and 'Authenticator confirmed. Now save your recovery codes.'

13.why: Show/hide toggles exist for the QR pattern, setup secret, and recovery codes, 'Request another code' re-issues the identity code, and no screen mentions penalties or attempt limits.

14.why: The only error observed, 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.', states the problem and the fix in neutral language without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or reading timer appears on any screen, but the 'page check expired' error shows a time-based expiry can still interrupt the flow, so the no-time-limit claim only mostly holds.
